original_value: AbstractBig data is one of the most recent business and technical issues in the age of technology. Hundreds of millions of events occur every day. The financial field is deeply involved in the calculation of big data events. As a result, hundreds of millions of financial transactions occur in the financial world each day. Therefore, financial practitioners and analysts consider it an emerging issue of the data management and analytics of different financial products and services. Also, big data has significant impacts on financial products and services. Therefore, identifying the financial issues where big data has a significant influence is also an important issue to explore with the influences. Based on these concepts, the objective of this paper was to show the current landscape of finance dealing with big data, and also to show how big data influences different financial sectors, more specifically, its impact on financial markets, financial institutions, and the relationship with internet finance, financial management, internet credit service companies, fraud detection, risk analysis, financial application management, and so on. The connection between big data and financial-related components will be revealed in an exploratory literature review of secondary data sources. Since big data in the financial field is an extremely new concept, future research directions will be pointed out at the end of this study.

result.paraphrase: Big data is among the newest business and technical challenges in the technology era. Every day, hundreds of millions of events and financial transactions take place, and finance is deeply tied to big-data processing. As a result, financial professionals and analysts view it as an emerging issue in data management and analytics across various financial products and services. Big data also has major effects on those products and services, making it important to identify the financial areas it influences most. Accordingly, this paper aims to present the current state of finance in relation to big data and to explain how big data affects different financial sectors—especially financial markets, financial institutions, internet finance, financial management, internet credit service companies, fraud detection, risk analysis, financial application management, and related areas. Using an exploratory literature review of secondary sources, it examines the links between big data and finance, and because this is an extremely new concept in the financial field, the study concludes by outlining directions for future research.
